title: 2000-10-26 10:26:20.00 — datum-zero anchor on the number line
role: 0d reference datum; both calendar renderings are divisor-rich and digit-sum-palindromic.

verification.shared_structure: 2^4 x 5^3 x p (two primes) -> (4+1)(3+1)(2)(2) = 80 divisors in both directions
verification.method: exact factorization + divisor count computed with integer arithmetic

exact_count_2000.parity_note: all 17 are even-month/even-day; the date (10,26) is one of them

year_2007_comparison.reading: the tau=80 both-orientation property is a trailing-000 (year-2000) artifact; tau=8 agreement is the generic small-tau coincidence

null_analysis.reading: rare among arbitrary 8-digit numbers; common within year-2000 (trailing 000 inflates tau >= 16); both-orientation agreement ~1 in 22. A mild, real coincidence, not a law.
null_analysis.clock_time_tau_note: tau(37580)=12 equals tau(60) and tau(260): the sexagesimal and tzolkin divisor counts.

base_invariance.test: tau-equality of the orientation pairs when the digit strings are re-encoded in bases 8, 10, 12, 16
base_invariance.reading: agreement survives decimal AND duodecimal encoding, breaks in octal and hexadecimal. Base-selective, not convention-free. Note that 12^2 = 144 and 10^2 = 100 are the two bases whose squares are divisor-rich.

scale_dependence.reading: tau-equality under MM/DD swap OSCILLATES with scale: holds at 2, 5, 6, 8 digits; breaks at 3, 4, 14. Not a systematic law; a scale-dependent coincidence.

8digit_digits_20001026.note: tau=8 is the mode among ALL permutations of the date's 8 digits; the 80-pair sits in a 3.6% family.

divisors_80.factor_shape: 2^4 x 5^3 x p x q (exponent signature 4,3,1,1) for both; p,q = 7,733 vs 31,421
divisors_80.gcd_note: the year itself is the greatest common divisor; the 20 shared divisors are exactly the divisors of 2000 (tau=20)
divisors_80.self_reference: the divisor count 80 divides both numbers (80 = 2^4 x 5 is a common divisor)

cross_scale_nesting.note: the 5-digit pair appears as divisors of the 8-digit pair (x1000); the retrace-chain members are divisors of the epoch

non_divisors.note: the day 26 does not divide either number (26 = 2x13, no factor 13); only the year 2000 and the trailing 1000 structure divide

note: Both orientations of the date share divisor count (80) and digit sum (11): the anchor is orientation-stable under MM/DD <-> DD/MM at several scales. See docs/WEAVERS_SCRIBE.md for the cultural mapping and the binding creases.
